A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PI-BSNet work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original PDE-learning experiments, recovery-probability comparisons, ablations, and additional Burgers and 3D heat results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds Neumann diffusion experiments, ICBC-enforcement ablations, derivative comparisons, and a loss/error analysis.

M1.justification: The coefficient network, B-spline representation, analytical derivatives, losses, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Neumann boundary penalties were already included in v2 Equation 10; the new experiments do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a one-dimensional diffusion family with varying diffusivity, a cosine initial condition, and Neumann conditions at both endpoints. This differs from the retained mixed-boundary 3D heat experiment. The existing PDE families and annulus reconstruction remain.

E2.justification: V3 adds PI-BSNet with loss-based ICBC enforcement as an explicit comparison variant in Appendix E.3, Table 3. Existing recovery-probability and 3D heat comparator membership is retained; the new Neumann experiment reuses PINN and PI-DeepONet.

E3.justification: Figure 4 switches from L2 error to relative L2 error; Sections 5.2, 5.3, and F.1 replace MSE/MAE reporting with relative L2 error. Added experiments introduce checkpoint-based testing, a 50-training/10-testing Neumann protocol with 5000 epochs, and controlled ICBC-loss comparisons. Rerunning the retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends analysis of the method's central components: direct versus penalty-based ICBC enforcement, derivative accuracy after fitting an analytical surface, and maximum prediction error versus training loss. It also adds inference timing to the control-point sensitivity study. Earlier noise, loss-weight, network-depth, and control-point-optimality analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 first reports a plus/minus uncertainty term for trapezoid prediction error, whereas v2 gives only aggregate MSE and MAE. Both versions specify 10 testing trials there. Existing repeated-run reporting remains; no increase in those run counts is established.

E6.justification: New v3 Table 1 reports Neumann PI-BSNet results of 148.6 seconds and 0.01932 relative L2 error, versus PINN's 914.4 seconds and 0.01697: faster but slightly less accurate. Table 3 reports errors of 0.0145 versus 0.0552 for direct versus penalty-based ICBC enforcement. Table 2 favors splines for first and mixed derivatives but finite differences for pure second derivatives; Table 4 adds inference times. Existing error results are replaced under different metrics, such as advection MSE 0.006178 becoming relative L2 error 0.1444, which does not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 removes the unexplained sigma-squared denominator from the final generalization bound, aligning v3 Equation 41 with the theorem. Appendix B.2 revises the multidimensional approximation proof using interval partitions and half-spacing bounds; B.3 adds qualifications to its sampling argument. The main theorem statements remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same principal claims about parametric PDE learning, direct IC/Dirichlet enforcement, analytical derivatives, theoretical guarantees, and efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. Added future directions do not constitute new achieved contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning parameter coverage and generalization, inference overhead, and sensitivity to ICBC-loss balancing. Appendix C.3 newly presents an advection loss/error trend as verification of Theorem 4.6, despite its stated elliptic/parabolic scope. Appendix F.1 removes the claim of comparability with published FNO results.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-access link, explicitly states that methods share test sets, and documents settings for the added experiments, including budgets, network widths, and loss weights. Disclosure remains incomplete: Appendix C.4 leaves the Neumann experiment's control-point count blank.

R1.justification: V3 expands the contrast with Wandel's fixed-parameter spline method, adds references on PINN loss pathologies, and removes the Tang polynomial-interpolation discussion. Proof references and attribution are also revised, including replacing Agmon with Evans and Pratt with Unser et al. The overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: There are targeted expansions in the introduction, related work, theory explanations, and discussion, plus new appendix subsections and publication/acknowledgment text. Duplicated Hilbert-space definitions are removed from the main text but retained in the appendix. Most prose and the overall section organization remain.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned to highlight direct ICBC assignment and analytical derivatives, and Figure 4 revises its error axis. The appendix gains a loss/error plot, Neumann comparisons, additional parameter-case visualizations, fitted-derivative panels, and ICBC comparisons with new tables. Retained displays are relocated and renumbered, and the control-point table gains an inference-time row.

improvement.justification: The controlled ICBC ablation provides evidence for a central design advantage that v2 did not isolate. The Neumann comparison, fitted-derivative analysis, proof refinements, and code link add useful support and reproducibility information. These gains remain limited by the missing control-point count in C.4 and C.3's use of advection to claim verification of a theorem stated only for elliptic/parabolic PDEs.
